ui.materialWizard.title: Material Wizard
ui.materialWizard.pageTitle: Material Wizard - A tool to create PBR materials for BeamNG
ui.materialWizard.tagline: A tool to create PBR materials for BeamNG. Photos are not uploaded to the server.
ui.materialWizard.drop: Click, drop or paste a photo to start.
ui.materialWizard.splitTip: Drag to make the preview wider or narrower. Double-click to reset.
ui.materialWizard.splitHeightTip: Drag to make the preview taller or shorter. Double-click to reset.
ui.materialWizard.zoomTip: Scroll over the picture to zoom. Drag to move it. Double-click to reset.
ui.materialWizard.presets.name: Preset name
ui.materialWizard.presets.tip: Load a saved preset. The photo and the material name stay as they are.
ui.materialWizard.presets.saveTip: Save the current settings under this name. Saving an existing name replaces it.
ui.materialWizard.maps.title: material
ui.materialWizard.maps.intro: Start with a photo. It is the base color, and the other maps are generated from it unless you load your own or set a flat value. A loaded height or normal feeds the maps that depend on it. Click a thumbnail to view it large.
ui.materialWizard.maps.previewSizeTip: Maps are worked on at this size while you edit, to save GPU memory.
ui.materialWizard.maps.shapeTip: Power-of-two photos keep their own ratio. Auto detects it.
ui.materialWizard.maps.colorTip: Multiplied with the base color texture and saved as baseColorFactor. Flat mode uses it as the whole color. White leaves a texture unchanged.
ui.materialWizard.maps.factorTip: Written to the material and multiplied with the map in the game. 1 keeps the map as it is.
ui.materialWizard.maps.orm: ORM (R ao, G rough, B metal)
ui.materialWizard.maps.rma: RMA (R rough, G metal, B ao)
ui.materialWizard.maps.lightsNote: 3 to 8 photos from a fixed camera, each with its own light direction. Solves the base color and a normal. For a scan you lit yourself.
ui.materialWizard.tile.title: tiling
ui.materialWizard.tile.offNote: Tiling is off. Turn on Tile this photo to use the frame.
ui.materialWizard.tile.intro: Tiling stays off until you turn it on. Drag the orange frame on the photo to pick the tile, and drag a corner to resize it. Switch to tile repeated above the picture to check the seams.
ui.materialWizard.tile.zoomTip: Scroll to zoom. Drag empty space, or the right mouse button, to move the picture. Double-click to reset.
ui.materialWizard.tile.highlightTip: Show or hide this edge's color, so you can see the blend.
ui.materialWizard.tile.edgesNote: An edge that is on gets covered with the photo from the dashed area past the opposite edge, so it matches when the tile repeats. One edge per direction is usually enough. With both on, each covers at half strength.
ui.materialWizard.tile.fitTip: Make the frame as big as the photo allows, leaving room for the sides that are on
ui.materialWizard.albedo.title: base color
ui.materialWizard.shape.title: height and normal
ui.materialWizard.shape.flip: DirectX normal (flip Y). BeamNG wants this off.
ui.materialWizard.shape.detailNote: For a soft photoscan bake: load the baked normal, then add fine detail from the photo on top of it.
ui.materialWizard.shape.addDetail: Add detail to the loaded normal
ui.materialWizard.shape.detailAuto: Match the amount to how soft the bake is
ui.materialWizard.shape.flatOnly: Only where the bake is flat
ui.materialWizard.shape.mapDetailAo: Add detail to the loaded AO
ui.materialWizard.shape.mapDetailRough: Add detail to the loaded roughness
ui.materialWizard.shape.mapDetailMetal: Add detail to the loaded metallic
ui.materialWizard.surface.title: surface
ui.materialWizard.surface.metalNote: Metallic comes from the zone materials. Use Flat on the Metallic map for one value everywhere.
ui.materialWizard.preview.hint: Drag turns the shape. Ctrl-drag, middle-drag or two fingers move it. Shift-drag or right-drag moves the sun. Scroll or pinch zooms. Double-click resets.
ui.materialWizard.preview.zoomTip: Scroll to zoom out or in. Double-click resets.
ui.materialWizard.preview.sunTip: Drag to place the sun. The centre is straight overhead, the bright ring is the horizon, and past it the sun sits below the horizon. The camera is at the bottom, so the top of the dial puts the sun in front of it. Scroll changes the height. Double-click resets.
ui.materialWizard.preview.hdr: The lit view is HDR on this screen. Highlights go up to {nits} nits.
ui.materialWizard.export.title: export
ui.materialWizard.export.name: Material name
ui.materialWizard.export.nameNote: The name comes from the photo you open. It names the zip and every saved map.
ui.materialWizard.export.saveNote: Save one map as a PNG:
ui.materialWizard.export.sizeNote: Used only when you save a map or the zip. The preview stays at the preview size.
ui.materialWizard.export.batchNote: Point at a folder. Each photo becomes a material with the settings on screen. A base color plus a matching normal is treated as a baked set.
ui.materialWizard.notes.stretch: Image aspect is far from the working size, so it is being stretched.
ui.materialWizard.notes.resampled: {name} was resampled to the working size.
ui.materialWizard.notes.road: Road width {width} m across the image. Set textureLength to {length} in the editor. Roughness {rough}, metallic {metal}.
ui.materialWizard.notes.tileMargin: Not enough photo beyond the frame for: {sides}. Move the frame, make it smaller or use Fit frame.
ui.materialWizard.notes.repeat: Repeat about {x} x {y} px. Crop {w} x {h}.
ui.materialWizard.notes.lengthFile: Set the road textureLength to {length} meters. Overlays need a higher renderPriority than the base road, set on the road in the editor.
ui.materialWizard.notes.objectSpace: Loaded normal looks object-space. This tool expects a tangent-space normal.
ui.materialWizard.notes.gpuCap: The photo is {w} x {h}. Previewing at {sw} x {sh} so it fits in GPU memory.
ui.materialWizard.notes.gpuOom: The GPU ran out of memory at {size} px. Working at up to {cap} px instead.
ui.materialWizard.notes.exportCap: Saved maps are {sw} x {sh}. The photo is {w} x {h}, which is larger than this GPU can hold.
ui.materialWizard.notes.gpuLost: The GPU ran out of memory and reset. Retrying at a smaller size.
ui.materialWizard.fix.rotateNote: Turn the photo until the lines in it follow the grid. Drag on the picture or use the slider. The picture is zoomed in a little, so no empty corners are left.
ui.materialWizard.fix.quadNote: Photographed at an angle? Drag the four corners onto something that should be a rectangle, like a paving slab or the edges of a road. The small view shows the result.
ui.materialWizard.fix.title: adjust
ui.materialWizard.fix.note: Straighten a tilted photo, correct the perspective of one taken at an angle, or crop it. The big view shows the whole photo while this tab is open. Apply changes the photo that every map is made from.
ui.materialWizard.fix.cropNote: Drag the frame to choose what stays. A shape keeps the frame at that ratio. Apply cuts the photo, and every loaded map, to the frame.
ui.materialWizard.albedo.fixNote: Removes the light and shadows of the photo so the base color is flat. Turn it off for a base color that is already clean, like a baked diffuse. Moving any slider below turns it on.
ui.materialWizard.presets.exportTip: Save the selected preset to a file. With no preset selected, all presets are saved.
ui.materialWizard.presets.importTip: Add presets from a .mwpreset.json file. Presets with the same name are replaced.
ui.materialWizard.albedo.unevenNote: Fixes a photo that is brighter on one side. Only the brightness changes, the colors stay. Brighten repeats across the tile, so it stays seamless.
ui.materialWizard.shape.gainTip: How strong the height is. Below 0 the height is inverted, so dents become bumps.
ui.materialWizard.shape.levelTip: Flattens slopes across the whole picture, which usually come from uneven light, and keeps the small detail.
ui.materialWizard.surface.zonesNote: The base material covers the whole photo. Add a zone to give parts with a different color (paint lines, moss, rust, metal) their own material. A pixel that matches no zone keeps the base material.
ui.materialWizard.surface.pickNote: Click the photo to pick the color.
ui.materialWizard.surface.rangeTip: How far a color may be from the picked one and still count. The edge is soft.
ui.materialWizard.albedo.shadowTip: Lifts only the dark areas that have the same color as their surroundings.
ui.materialWizard.albedo.lightColorsNote: Pick the colors of the material whose lighting should be measured, such as the gravel but not the grass. The range and the amount appear once a color is picked. Only those colors decide how bright each area is. Everything else is corrected by its neighbors. Also used by Even out brightness and contrast before tiling.
ui.materialWizard.albedo.lightAmountTip: How strongly the picked colors are evened. Works on its own, without Lighting correction.
ui.materialWizard.albedo.autoTip: Balances the mid-tones toward gray. Highlights, deep shadows and strong colors are skipped.
ui.materialWizard.tile.even: Even out brightness and contrast before tiling
ui.materialWizard.notes.newerFile: This file was made with version {v}. Some settings may be ignored.
ui.materialWizard.notes.saveFailed: The project could not be verified, so nothing was saved.
ui.materialWizard.adjust.title: Adjust
ui.materialWizard.adjust.curveTip: Drag a point up or down, or use the arrow keys. Double-click to reset.
ui.materialWizard.surface.localRoughTip: Rougher where the base color changes over a small area
ui.materialWizard.tile.viewRepeatTip: Highlights areas that appear more than once in the tile
ui.materialWizard.tile.bombTip: Copies soft-edged patches of the tile to other places. The edges stay seamless, and loaded maps get the same patches.
ui.materialWizard.export.patternTip: {prefix}, {name} and {n}, the number in a batch. {n:02} pads it to two digits.
ui.materialWizard.export.copyFailed: Could not copy. The browser blocked the clipboard.
ui.materialWizard.alphaViewTip: What shows through the transparent parts of the material
ui.materialWizard.terrain.baseNote: The base layer is the terrain base texture that is seen from far away. The game makes it from the terrain, so here it is either the average color of this material or the material itself.
ui.materialWizard.terrain.blendTip: Shows a gray layer in a checker pattern, mixed by height like in the game.
ui.materialWizard.terrain.distTip: The map fades in between the first two distances and fades out between the last two.
ui.materialWizard.terrain.attenTip: How much of the strength is kept close to the camera (near) and far away (far).
ui.materialWizard.terrain.groundmodelTip: Ground model name from the game, for example GRASS, DIRT, ASPHALT or SAND.
ui.materialWizard.terrain.exportNote: Terrain export saves detail maps (t_name_b, _nm, _r, _ao, _h) recentred on 0.5, smaller macro maps (t_macro_name_*) and a TerrainMaterial entry in main.materials.json.
ui.materialWizard.terrain.layerNote: Each layer has its own photo and settings. A layer without a photo is taken from the other one.
